name: Mimi-Gaudefroy
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Attested only via Gaudefroy-Demombynes 1907 wordlist (Decorse); no phonological description exists.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2021 (draft). The Maban languages and their place within Nilo-Saharan.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Mimi-D prosody; only classificatory remarks ('The issue of Mimi is unresolved. There are three sources, Decorse (1907), Lukas & Völckers (1939) and Jungraithmayr (1971).. Decorse's Mimi is almost certainly a Maban group language').

sources.citation: Starostin, George. 2011. On Mimi. Journal of Language Relationship 6: 115-140.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. States that the only Mimi-D data is Decorse's list in Gaudefroy-Demombynes 1907: 322-329; remarks only on segmental matters (e.g. 'Decorse did not indicate the presence of nasalized vowels in his Mimi'; unclear value of the dot in Decorse's transcription, fn. 5).

sources.citation: Gaudefroy-Demombynes, Maurice. 1907. Documents sur les langues de l'Oubangui-Chari. In: Actes du XIVe Congrès international des orientalistes, Alger 1905, Partie 2 (Quatrième section: Égypte, langues africaines), pp. 172-330. Paris: E. Leroux. Section XI 'Mimi', pp. 322-330.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only phonological remark is the general transcription note on p. 174: 'Les transcriptions n'ont aucune précision : toutes les consonnes gardent leur son normal et isolé; š = ch, č = tch, ǰ = dj : u = ou, o = o ouvert et ô = o fermé.' The Mimi section (pp. 322-330) is an introduction on the people (Nachtigal III p. 191 cited), an alphabetical French-Mimi wordlist of ca. 200 items with comparative notes, and numerals 1-10; no grammar, no accent/stress/tone statement. Grave/circumflex marks in a few forms (mèl, kyedô, lékèk, tèlit, lôsu, rèp, nâges) are vowel-quality marks per p. 17…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page mimi1240 'Mimi-Gaudefroy' and reference records 17699 (Gaudefroy-Demombynes 1907), 312985 (Decorse 1906), 139914 (Starostin 2011)
sources.note: No stress content; confirms the language is known from a single wordlist and lists exactly three references (wordlist, expedition account, comparative article). Glottolog 5.1 export in had 0 descriptive refs.

sources.citation: Decorse, Gaston Jules. 1906. Du Congo au lac Tchad: la brousse telle qu'elle est, les gens tels qu'ils sont, carnet de route. Paris: Asselin & Houzeau. vii+347 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; the travelogue contains zero occurrences of 'Mimi' and no linguistic appendix. Glottolog lists it as a Mimi-Gaudefroy reference only as the account of the expedition on which the wordlist was collected.
Nothing; repeats that the language is known only from Decorse's wordlist in Gaudefroy-Demombynes 1907 and Starostin's 2011 re-analysis.
